sources.label: U.S. National Science Board / NCSES — Discovery: R&D Activity and Research Publications
sources.note: Scopus-indexed S&E publication output: 2.0M in 2010, 3.117M in 2021, 3.275M in 2023.

sources.label: Nature — More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023
sources.note: 2023 passed 10,000 retractions; most of the exceptional spike came from Hindawi cleanup.

sources.label: Nature — Retractions are increasing, but not enough
sources.note: About 45 retractions/month in 2010, nearly 300/month in 2021; commentary estimates roughly 1 in 50 papers could meet at least one COPE retraction criterion while observed retraction remained below 0.1% at the time.

sources.label: Aczel et al. — A billion-dollar donation: estimating the cost of researchers' time spent on peer review
sources.note: More than 100 million reviewer hours globally in 2020, equivalent to more than 15,000 24-hour years; estimates are intentionally conservative.

sources.label: Freedman, Cockburn & Simcoe — The Economics of Reproducibility in Preclinical Research
sources.note: Estimated more than 50% cumulative irreproducibility in US preclinical life science and about $28B/year in direct spending associated with irreproducible work; this is not a global all-discipline estimate.

sources.label: Hsiao & Schneider — Continued use of retracted papers
sources.note: Among 13,252 post-retraction citation contexts, only 722 (5.4%) acknowledged the retraction.

sources.label: Fanelli — How Many Scientists Fabricate and Falsify Research?
sources.note: 2009 meta-analysis: 1.97% self-reported fabrication/falsification/modification at least once; up to 33.7% self-reported other questionable practices. These are survey prevalence estimates, not paper-level fraud rates.

sources.label: Nature — Stamp out paper mills
sources.note: Cites an estimate that at least 400,000 papers published 2000–2022 show paper-mill hallmarks.

sources.label: Porter & McIntosh — Identifying fabricated networks within authorship-for-sale enterprises
sources.note: Reports an estimate that about 2% of journal submissions across disciplines originate from paper mills.
